{{Short description|British mathematician (1904–1968)}}
'''Leonard Roth''' (29 August 1904 – 28 November 1968) was a mathematician working in the [[Italian school of algebraic geometry]]. He introduced an example of a [[unirational variety]] that was not rational (though his proof that it was not rational was incomplete).

Roth was born in [[Edmonton, London]]. He was educated at [[Latymer Upper School]], [[Dulwich College]] and [[Clare College, Cambridge]], where he graduated as a [[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|Wrangler]] in 1926.<ref>John J. O'Connor and [[Edmund F. Robertson]], [http://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Roth.html "Leonard Roth"], ''[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]''. Accessed 20 April 2020.</ref> He died in 1968 in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]]. His sister was [[Queenie Roth]], literary critic and wife of [[F. R. Leavis]].
